channel.description: Recent content in Organic Life on Dipesh Dulal's Blog

item.title: Berry-picking and Theory of Multiple Intelligence
item.description: Berry-picking activity could we well related to theory of multiple intelligence.

item.title: Iskus ko Munta: Tender Chayote Shoots - Vegetable in Abundance
item.description: Chayote gourd had been a readily available source of food in Nepal. Somehow forgotten, chayote (‘Iskus’ in Nepali) has been mighty in my garden.

item.title: I Tried Ban Silam Seeds
item.description: When it comes to nutritional- and/or health benefits of some random herbs as suggested by social circles, Nepalese people tend to run for it. So did I for ban silam seeds.

item.title: We cooked air potato!
item.description: Our grandparents ate this, why can’t we? - said my mom. While trying the aerial tuber of this climber, I parallelly researched more about it and found that some varieties are toxic!

item.title: South American Pepino Growing on my Nepali Garden
item.description: It is all about sharing and caring: I got a branch of pepino melon plant from a friend and have been sharing the overgrown twigs to enthusiastic gardeners.

item.title: Nepali Kade Dhaniya (Culantro)
item.description: Culantro has already been localized with Nepali names (Kade Dhaniya, Ban Dhaniya, and so on) though it is believed to originate in the Americas.

item.title: We collect Lamb's Quarters (Bethe ko Sag)
item.description: Bethe ko Sag (Lamb’s Quarters) can be promising alternative food for the world while Nepalese have been cooking it since eternity.
